items.headline: Greed falls to 74 while Valuation rises to 89
items.summary: The live AGCI engine moved to Greed 74/100, down 10 points daily and 4 over seven days, while Valuation reached 89/100. Regime remains Correction but the matrix de-escalated to PRICE_DISCIPLINE / Wait / Price discipline.
items.whyItMatters: Sentiment has reset meaningfully from euphoria, but valuation is more extreme; improved entry optionality does not justify chasing beta.

items.headline: Oil retreat stabilizes Treasuries after multi-decade yield highs
items.summary: Treasury yields stabilized Friday as oil fell on renewed U.S.-Iran deal hopes, after benchmark yields had reached fresh multi-decade highs. Markets still price further Federal Reserve tightening.
items.whyItMatters: Lower oil reduces near-term inflation pressure, but the rate regime remains restrictive and keeps the hurdle rate high for long-duration equities and real estate.

items.headline: Equities rebound despite 10Y near 5.2%; Iran hopes drive Friday risk-on
items.summary: Barron's reported the S&P 500 up 0.5% Friday and 1.2% for the week, with the Nasdaq up 2.1% weekly, even as the 10-year Treasury yield reached roughly 5.18%. Friday's move was helped by renewed hopes for progress in U.S.-Iran talks and lower oil.
items.whyItMatters: Risk assets are discounting a transitory rates/energy shock; with valuation extreme, AGCI requires confirmed diplomatic and inflation progress before increasing beta.

items.headline: Biotech bull case broadens on innovation and M&A
items.summary: Barron's weekend issue highlights accelerating biotech performance supported by medical innovation and renewed merger activity, while also flagging company-specific opportunities across healthcare.
items.whyItMatters: Biotech can diversify AI-heavy equity exposure, but AGCI would favor catalyst-backed pipelines and balance-sheet durability over broad momentum chasing.

items.headline: AI monetization broadens while valuation discipline remains critical
items.summary: Barron's weekend coverage highlights Meta Muse, Microsoft Copilot monetization, data-center power constraints and continued AI-linked stock dispersion. The signal is broader commercialization, not uniform economics.
items.whyItMatters: AGCI continues to require customer concentration, power availability, inference cost, margins, security and free-cash-flow evidence before capitalizing AI narratives.
